short: The bloodiest battle in Scandinavian history, which secured Swedish control of Scania.
full:
Fought on 4 December 1676, the Battle of Lund was the decisive engagement of the Scanian War. The Swedish army, commanded by the young King Charles XI, met a slightly larger Danish force under King Christian V just north of Lund. The battle commenced early in the morning with a chaotic cavalry clash in the dark, leading to hours of brutal, disorganized combat across freezing terrain.

The engagement escalated into an incredibly bloody stalemate before a final Swedish cavalry charge broke the Danish lines late in the afternoon. Casualty rates were extraordinarily high; roughly half of the 21,000 men engaged were killed or wounded. Although tactically a pyrrhic victory, it proved strategically vital. The defeat broke the momentum of the Danish invasion, permanently cementing Swedish dominion over the fiercely contested province of Scania.
